title: Giving change
examples: If I pay with a ten dollar bill, how much change should I get back?
Can you show me how to count up to the amount I paid?
What is the difference between paying and getting change?

explain.say: Today we learn about giving change with money. Change is the money you get back. You get change when you pay more than the cost.
We can find the change by counting up. Start at the price and count up to the amount you paid. Each number is the change.

items: Count up to the amount paid

draw.text: Count up to the amount paid

explain.say: For example, if a toy costs three dollars. You pay with five dollars. We count up: three to four, four to five. You get two dollars change.
We can also use subtraction to find the change. Take the amount paid and subtract the cost. This gives you the change amount.
Let us try another example. If a book costs four dollars. You pay with ten dollars. We subtract ten minus four. The change is six dollars.

faq.a: Change is the extra money you receive when you pay with more than the actual price. It is the difference between what you paid and what something cost.
No, you can use either counting up or subtraction. Both methods help you find the correct amount of change.
asks: Is counting up the only way?

faq.q: When do I need to calculate change?
faq.a: You need to calculate change when the money you give is more than the price of the item. This happens at shops and stores.

faq.q: If I pay with a ten dollar bill, how do I know the change?
faq.a: You can count up from the price to ten dollars. For example, if it costs seven dollars, you count up seven to eight, eight to nine, nine to ten. You get three dollars change.
asks: How do I count up to ten?
What if I pay with a twenty dollar bill?

faq.q: Is subtraction always easier for change?
faq.a: It depends on what you are comfortable with. Subtraction is quick for simple numbers, while counting up is good for visualizing the steps.

facts: Change is the money returned after a purchase.
Counting up involves starting at the price and counting to the paid amount.
Subtraction finds the difference between two numbers.
If the paid amount equals the cost, you get zero change.

quiz.say: A pencil costs two dollars. You pay with five dollars. How much change do you get?
quiz.why: You subtract the cost from the amount paid, so five minus two equals three dollars.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you cannot subtract a number from itself.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you added the two numbers together instead of subtracting.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you are subtracting the numbers instead of finding the difference.

quiz.say: A snack costs four dollars. You pay with ten dollars. How much change is correct?
quiz.why: Counting up from four to ten gives you six dollars in change.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you subtracted the cost from the change amount.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you only wrote down the original cost.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you added the two numbers together instead of finding the difference.

quiz.say: If an item costs eight dollars, and you pay with twenty dollars, what is the change?
quiz.why: Using subtraction, twenty minus eight equals twelve dollars change.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you subtracted eight from twenty, but forgot to count up.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you added the two numbers together.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only subtracted the tens digit.
